subject: Discovery: PII handling, retention & audit logging — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emma Dawson <emma.dawson@finservcorp.com>, Ben Howard <ben.howard@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention, and audit logging (next steps)

Hi Emma / Ben —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we can align on next steps and make sure we capture your compliance constraints accurately. If I missed anything, please flag.

Pain points you shared:
- Sensitive customer PII flows into your product via ingestion pipelines (payment info, SSNs in specific forms).
- Current vendor stack (in-house inference + ad-hoc logging) has inconsistent redaction and retention policies across services.
- Audits take too long because logs are noisy and lack structured audit events tied to user IDs.

Current stack you described:
- Model inference running on self-managed GPU fleet (K8s)
- Logging into Splunk with custom parsers
- SIEM for alerts and quarterly compliance reviews

Success criteria for a vendor solution (prioritized):
1) Zero-PHI/PII persistence unless explicitly allowed (configurable redaction at request/response boundary).
2) Per-request audit logs that are tamper-evident and include routing/model version metadata.
3) Retention controls by data type and by customer (able to TTL tokens/logs down to N days).
4) SOC-2/ISO-friendly artifacts for audit teams and an easy way to hand over requested evidence.

Constraints/requirements you emphasized:
- Retention: log retention must be configurable by policy (30/90/365 days) per customer.
- Redaction: ability to auto-redact fields matching regexes and to provide deterministic hashes for linking without revealing raw PII.
- Audit logs: immutable indexes for user-level events, exportable on demand for auditors.
- Data residency: primary requirement is US-only storage for production logs.

Proposed immediate next steps (to keep momentum):
1) I will share a short security questionnaire (attached) with specific fields about log schemas and redaction hooks — please review and return with any notes by EOD Wed (3/3).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your platform/sec engineering (30–45 minutes) — Monica, can you propose two windows next week?
3) If questionnaire looks good, we can prepare a demo of redaction + audit export using a synthetic dataset and show TTL controls.

Attachments: rfi_security_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet) — short set of targeted questions; redaction_examples.png (image) — sample redaction options we discussed.

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198
From: Emma Dawson <emma.dawson@finservcorp.com>

Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — PII handling, retention, and audit logging (next steps)

Thanks Karthik — this lines up with what we discussed. A few clarifications / additions: 

1) Retention specifics: our legal/controls team currently enforces 90 days for telemetry logs and 7 years for transactional records; for PII we try to minimize storage and prefer hashed/ephemeral approaches.
2) Redaction: deterministic hashing for linking is good — but we need a way to demonstrate to auditors that original values are unrecoverable.
3) Access controls: audit exports should indicate which Redwood user/service accessed logs (IAM principal) and include timestamps with timezone normalization.
4) PCI/SOC overlap: our payments team will want PCI scope minimization — anything that helps keep raw card data out of vendor logs is a plus.

We can have our infra/security engineers join the tech deep-dive. I can propose times on Monday/Tuesday. We'll look at the short questionnaire and try to get answers back within 48 hours.

—Emma

Can you review the attached RFI (rfi_security_questions.xlsx) and reply with:
- Whether our current Dedicated offering supports per-customer TTL on logs and how that is enforced (storage layer / lifecycle policy).
- Recommended approaches for deterministic non-reversible hashing we can ship without expanding threat model (HMAC with customer-managed salt? key rotation implications?).
- Whether our audit logs are currently tamper-evident and exportable in the format auditors request (CSV + signed manifest). If not, quick estimate of work to support signed manifests.

Proposed timeline: security review comments back by Tue EOD (3/2), technical deep-dive with their engineers Wed/Thu next week. Monica — can you lock 2 x 30-min windows on Wed/Thu?
